notes: Normal all-feature musl release. Nine retained-daemon points request 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 21G each way, then unlimited. CPU placement, QinQ traffic, active PMTU and the 1500-byte outer ceiling match the preceding 60-second comparison. No builds, other tests or Git packing overlap load.

Both directions have under 1% missing through 2G offered; 3G loses 21.03/18.07%. This is one ascending sweep, not repeated acceptance or a zero-loss ceiling. Retained controller state tests adaptation as well as steady forwarding.

Unlimited goodput falls 17.22% forward and 4.77% reverse from the 4G point; reverse peaks at 8G and falls 5.45% from that peak. From the preceding 21G point it falls 8.23/3.72%. No overload plateau is established.

All points have zero receiver invalid/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run/reordered records, admission pressure, socket overflow/errors, TAP errors, malformed packets, inner UDP errors and outer IPv6 fragmentation.

At 0.5G and 1G there are no TAP TX drops, but reverse missing is 0.42/0.43%; expiry and non-ACK queue drops are already nonzero. No single counter establishes exact causal attribution. ACK-buffer drops are included in queue_drops; units differ.

Goodput excludes drain; missing ratios and counter deltas include drain. 100% CPU is one core. Current runtime selective repair is still absent; its absence does not explain away scheduling and overload defects.
